title: Dreams & Dream Interpretations (Part 3)
arabic:
عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ رُؤْيَا النَّبِيِّ، صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ قَالَ ‏"‏ رَأَيْتُ النَّاسَ اجْتَمَعُوا فَقَامَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ فَنَزَعَ ذَنُوبًا أَوْ ذَنُوبَيْنِ، وَفِي نَزْعِهِ ضَعْفٌ وَاللَّهُ يَغْفِرُ لَهُ، ثُمَّ قَامَ ابْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، فَاسْتَحَالَتْ غَرْبًا فَمَا رَأَيْتُ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَفْرِي فَرْيَهُ، حَتَّى ضَرَبَ النَّاسُ بِعَطَنٍ ‏"

فَاسْتَحَالَتْ غَرْبًا فَمَا رَأَيْتُ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَفْرِي فَرْيَهُ، حَتَّى ضَرَبَ النَّاسُ بِعَطَنٍ الرجل الذي ليس فوق شئ سيد القوم كبيرهم وقويهم

‏"‏ بَيْنَا أَنَا نَائِمٌ أُتِيتُ بِقَدَحِ لَبَنٍ، فَشَرِبْتُ مِنْهُ، حَتَّى إِنِّي لأَرَى الرِّيَّ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَظْفَارِي، ثُمَّ أَعْطَيْتُ فَضْلِي ‏"‏‏.‏ يَعْنِي عُمَرَ‏.‏ قَالُوا فَمَا أَوَّلْتَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْعِلْمَ ‏"‏‏.‏

عن سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيَّ، يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ بَيْنَمَا أَنَا نَائِمٌ رَأَيْتُ النَّاسَ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَىَّ، وَعَلَيْهِمْ قُمُصٌ، مِنْهَا مَا يَبْلُغُ الثَّدْىَ، وَمِنْهَا مَا يَبْلُغُ دُونَ ذَلِكَ، وَمَرَّ عَلَىَّ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَعَلَيْهِ قَمِيصٌ يَجُرُّهُ ‏"‏‏.‏

قال أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ بَيْنَا نَحْنُ جُلُوسٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ بَيْنَا أَنَا نَائِمٌ رَأَيْتُنِي فِي الْجَنَّةِ، فَإِذَا امْرَأَةٌ تَتَوَضَّأُ إِلَى جَانِبِ قَصْرٍ، قُلْتُ لِمَنْ هَذَا الْقَصْرُ قَالُوا لِعُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ‏.‏ فَذَكَرْتُ غَيْرَتَهُ فَوَلَّيْتُ مُدْبِرًا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ فَبَكَى عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَعَلَيْكَ بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَغَارُ

إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ اللَّيْلَةَ فِي الْمَنَامِ ظُلَّةً تَنْطِفُ السَّمْنَ وَالْعَسَلَ، فَأَرَى النَّاسَ يَتَكَفَّفُونَ مِنْهَا فَالْمُسْتَكْثِرُ وَالْمُسْتَقِلُّ

وَإِذَا سَبَبٌ وَاصِلٌ مِنَ الأَرْضِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَأَرَاكَ أَخَذْتَ بِهِ فَعَلَوْتَ، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَعَلاَ بِهِ، ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَعَلاَ بِهِ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَانْقَطَعَ ثُمَّ وُصِلَ

وَسَأُحَدِّثُكَ لِمَ ذَاكَ رَأَيْتُ رُؤْيَا عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَصَصْتُهَا عَلَيْهِ، وَرَأَيْتُ كَأَنِّي فِي رَوْضَةٍ ـ ذَكَرَ مِنْ سَعَتِهَا وَخُضْرَتِهَا ـ وَسْطَهَا عَمُودٌ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ، أَسْفَلُهُ فِي الأَرْضِ وَأَعْلاَهُ فِي السَّمَاءِ، فِي أَعْلاَهُ عُرْوَةٌ فَقِيلَ لَهُ ارْقَهْ‏.‏ قُلْتُ لاَ أَسْتَطِيعُ‏.‏ فَأَتَانِي مِنْصَفٌ فَرَفَعَ ثِيَابِي مِنْ خَلْفِي، فَرَقِيتُ حَتَّى كُنْتُ فِي أَعْلاَهَا، فَأَخَذْتُ بِالْعُرْوَةِ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ اسْتَمْسِكْ‏.‏ فَاسْتَيْقَظْتُ وَإِنَّهَا لَفِي يَدِي، فَقَصَصْتُهَا عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

رَأَيْتُ رُؤْيَا لَا أُرَاهَا إِلَّا لِحُضُورِ أَجَلِي رَأَيْتُ كَأَنَّ دِيكًا نَقَرَنِي نَقْرَتَيْنِ قَالَ وَذَكَرَ لِي أَنَّهُ دِيكٌ أَحْمَرُ

كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُّسَنَّدَةٌ ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً ۚ لَأَسْقَيْنَـٰهُم مَّآءً غَدَقًالِّنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ

أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ

At’Ta’wīl bil hadīth (التأويل بالحديث): Qawarīr (قوارير): رفقًا بالقوارير Bāb ta’wīl Ru’yāt al Amtār :(باب تأويل رؤية الامطار)
english:
As I mentioned in the beginning of these talks that the righteous dream is that you see or someone else sees for you.

Dreams of Rasūlullāh ﷺ for Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه  and ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه: So here Rasūlullāh ﷺ saw dreams for Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه  and ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. In Sahīh Al-Bukhārī (صحيح البخاري), there's a Hadīth (حديث),

Rasūlullāh ﷺ saw a dream for Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه and ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, he saw that Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه  was pulling out water from a well, he was pulling out the bucket and he pulled out the bucket once or twice and Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, وَفِي نَزْعِهِ ضَعْفٌ, and his pulling was weak

وَاللَّهُ يَغْفِرُ لَهُ، and may Allāh ﷻ forgive him but when ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه started to pull out the water, Rasūlullāhﷺ  said, فَاسْتَحَالَتْ غَرْبًا، gharb is a huge bucket that is made from leather from cow hide.

He pulled out so much water until all the people brought their cattle, their camels to drink. And in another hadīth (حديث) that says that he is عبقري, abkarī, now in the current standard Arabic is used to refer to the genius but if we look at the origin of the word of abkari عبقري)), as was said by some of the scholars of Arabic, is the man who's at the top and there's no one above him,

and it's also used to refer to It is used to refer to the leader of his people or the strongest men among them. And this comes from the word ‘abkar (عبقر) and ‘abkar is a place where they used to make some particular type of cloth. Apparently, it was some special cloth and it is also a name of a place or a valley that was known for its Jinn (جن). So, it's the land of Jinn (جن), the land of Jinn (جن), was called upon and it was then used to refer to anything that is unique or special. So, anything that is unique or special, would be called ‘abkarī.

Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه  has a higher status than ‘‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه: Rasūlullāh ﷺ said that ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه is ‘Abkarī, in this hadith. what does this hadith mean? What does this dream mean? Obviously, we know that in terms of status and in terms of good deeds, Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه  has a higher status than ‘‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه . So how come here Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه  was pulling this bucket and there was weakness in his pulling, while with ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, it turned into a huge bucket and water was flowing. This hadith is not referring to status and ākhirah (اٰخرة), this hadīth (حديث) is referring to the khilāfah (خلافة) of Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه on the khilāfah (خلافة) of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, the khilāfah (خلافة) of Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was short in time, it was only for two years, and that's why he pulled out the bucket once or twice, but the khilāfah (خلافة) of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه lasted for 10 years. And the people that became Muslim through the conquest that occurred in the time of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, the masses that benefited from the reign of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, is huge compared to the Khilafah of Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, da’wah (دعوة) and time of Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was weak because Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was focused on fighting the Murtadīn (مرتدين) and bringing back the people who were already Muslim back to Islam. And in terms of time, it was only for two years but in the time of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, the foundation was set and established by Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه and now ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه spread the Da’wah (دعوة) in the east and the west. So, this is the interpretation of the dream of Rasūlullāh ﷺ that he had for Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه and ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه.

Milk Interpretated as Knowledge: In another hadīth (حديث), Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, This hadīth (حديث) in Bukhārī (بخاري), Rasūlullāh ﷺ said that he saw himself in his dream, drinking milk from Qadah (قدح), qadah (قدح) is a vessel made out of wood, Rasūlullāh ﷺ drank so much of this milk that he saw it coming out from beneath his nails. So, from the fingertips of Rasūlullāh ﷺ, milk was coming out, and then there were a little bit of milk left in this vessel. Rasūlullāh ﷺ gave it to ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه to drink, they said, what is the interpretation of this? He said, it is knowledge. So, milk here represents knowledge.

Using Symbols to Interpret Dreams: Rasūlullāh ﷺ said in this hadīth (حديث) in Bukhārī (بخاري), that people were presented to him wearing garments, some of them, the garment would reach to their breasts, and some of them a bit longer. And then ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه past in front of me, wearing a garment that he was dragging behind him. You might say, well, the Sunnah (سنة), is to have your garment above the ankle and here ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه is dragging his garment behind him, we said that dreams are not for legislation. They don't give us give us kind of Sharī’ah (شريعة). We see symbols and dreams that mean something, ya’nī, for example here it's not literally that ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه is wearing a garment that is dragging behind them. Because Rasūlullāh ﷺ gave us the interpretation, he said the interpretation of the garments, is the religion. So, everyone's religion is according to the garment that he was wearing. Some people their religion is very weak and that's why Rasūlullāh ﷺ saw the garment reaching to their breast. Some of them longer meaning their Dīn (دين) is stronger but the Dīn (دين) of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was so strong that his garment was being dragged, behind him.

Palace of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه in Jannah: Also, in Bukhārī (بخاري), In this hadīth (حديث), Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, I entered Jannah (جنة), I saw a woman making Wudhu (وضو), next to a palace so I asked who does this palace belong to? In this hadīth (حديث), it is summarized but another Hadīth (حديث), Rasūlullāh ﷺ asked the angels who does this palace belong to? they said it belongs to an ‘Arab man. The palace was so beautiful, So Rasūlullāh ﷺ might have thought that belongs to him. So, he said I am an ‘Arab man. They said it belongs to a man from Quraysh (قريش). Rasūlullāh ﷺ said I am from Quraysh, who does it belong to? they said it belongs to ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه.

Ghīrah (غيرة) of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه: Rasūlullāh ﷺ says in this Hadīth (حديث) that he asked the angels who does this palace belong to? they said it belongs to ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, so I remembered your Ghīrah (غيرة), Ghīrah is the jealousy that the person has for his woman, the protection that the man gives to his woman. Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, then I remembered ‘Umar’s ghīrah and I went back hurriedly. Rasūlullāh ﷺ left immediately because he remembered the ghīrah of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه weeped and said, let my father and mother be sacrificed for you, Oh messenger of Allāh! How dare I think of my Ghīrah being offended by you? These are some dreams that Rasūlullāh ﷺ, had of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه and Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه .

In our next section, we'll talk about the dreams of the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم, some dreams of the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم .

The first and this is in Bukhārī (بخاري). By the way, notice that a lot of the ahadīth (أحاديث) that we are mentioning, are from Bukhari, because Bukhari has an entire section or chapter in his Sahīh (صحيح) about dreams.

Rasūlullāh ﷺ would ask Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم about their Dreams: ‘Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه says that Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم would see dreams during the lifetime of Rasūlullāh ﷺ and then they would narrate their dreams to Rasūlullāh ﷺ and Rasūlullāh ﷺ would interpret the dreams for them. And at the time, Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was young, he was a bachelor and he would spend his time in Masjid (مسجد), he would sleep at the masjid and he told himself if there's any good in me, then I too will see a dream just like everybody else is seeing dreams. So, because the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم were seeing dreams, he wanted also to see a dream like them. So, one night when he went to bed, he made the du’ā (دعا), He said, Oh Allāh! if you see any good in me, show me a good dream. It's okay to ask Allāh to see a dream. This is what Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه did over here.

Dream of ‘Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه: He slept that night and Allāh ﷻ accepted his du’ā (دعا). He saw in his dream two angels come to him, but in the hands of each one of them there was a maze of iron and they grabbed him and they were taking him towards hell. Obviously Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was so terrified with this, so he made du’ā (دعا), He said, oh Allāh! I seek refuge in You from hell. Then he was faced by another angel. And this angel told him to not be afraid you will be an excellent man if you only pray more often. Obviously, this is talking about voluntary Salah (صلاة), nawāfil (نوافل), not the obligatory ones because every Sahābī used to pray the five daily prayers This is talking about Qiyām ul Layl (قيام الليل), the Nawāfil.

So, they took him and stopped him at the edge of hell. He said it looked like a well, could be a building that is usually built around a well, because in the old days when they would dig a well, they would line it with rocks so that the well wouldn't fall in. So, you saw that Hellfire looked like that. And he looked inside, and he saw some people that he knew from Quraysh (قريش), some of the kuffār (كفار) of Quraysh (قريش). And then the angels took him away. Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said I narrated this dream to Hafsah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها, his sister and the wife of Rasūlullāh ﷺ, and she narrated it to Rasūlullāh ﷺ and Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, no doubt, Abdullāh is a good man, if he would only pray more often. since that was told to Abdullāh bin ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, he would never leave Qiyām ul Layl (قيم الليل), and he would pray a lot at night.

Dream regarding Cloud raining butter and honey: In another dream, that was seen by one of the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم, this man came to Rasūlullāh ﷺ, and said,

this companion came to Rasūlullāh ﷺ, He said that I had a dream where I saw a cloud and this cloud was raining butter and honey. And then I saw people opening their hands and collecting from this butter and honey that is falling from this cloud. Some of them gathered a lot and some of them gathered a smaller amount. So, people were different. And then he said,

and then I saw a rope extending from earth to the heavens.

I saw you hold on to that rope, and then you went up, so Rasūlullāh ﷺ held on to that rope and it took him up to the heavens. And then another man held it and it went up. And then another man held it and it went up and then another man held it, but it broke, then it got connected again. So, after Rasūlullāh ﷺ there are three people who hold on to this rope but it broke with the third person however, it was connected again. And then he went up.

Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was an Interpreter of Dreams: So, Rasūlullāh ﷺ gave the interpretation of this dream, Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه interjected and said, O Messenger of Allāh! Allow me to interpret it. As we said, Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was an interpreter of dreams. And Rasūlullāh ﷺ told him to go ahead. Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said the cloud represents Islam and the butter and honey dropping from, it symbolises Qur’ān (قرآن), its sweetness dropping and some people learning much of Qur’ān (قرآن) and some people a little. So according to how much a person took from that butter and honey, that is how much they benefited from Qur’ān (قرآن) and the rope which is extending from sky to Earth is the truth, Al- ‘Urwah Al-Wuthqā (العروة الوثقىٰ) mentioned in the Qur’ān (قرآن), is the truth (الحق). So, you will hold on to it and it will rise you up. And then another person will hold on to it and he will rise up and then a third person will hold on to it and he will rise up and then the last person, it will break but then it will be connected for him and he will rise up with it. Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه now asked Rasūlullāh ﷺ and told him, am I right? And Rasūlullāh ﷺ told him, some of it was right, and some of it was wrong. Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said, O Messenger of Allāh! by Allāh, in the Name of Allāh, you must tell me in what I was wrong? Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was eager to know what his mistake was so that it's he wants to learn something new. Rasūlullāh ﷺ told him, do not swear. Rasūlullāh ﷺ refused to tell him what the mistake was.

The scholars after that explain the interpretation of this dream to mean, Al-Khīlafah (الخلافة), or the rule over the Muslims, first Rasūlullāh ﷺ was ruling over the Muslims until he passed away, and then the khilāfah (خلافة) of Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, and then the khilafah of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه and then the Khalifah of ‘Uthmān رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. So, the breaking of the rope represents the fitnah (فتنة) that occurred, but then Allāh ﷻ raised ‘Uthmān رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه.

Glad Tiding given to ‘Abdullāh bin salām رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه: Qais bin ‘Ubād رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, he is one of the Tabi’īn (تابعين), He said and this also is in Bukhārī (بخاري). He said that he was sitting with some Tabi’īn (تابعين) in the Masjid (مسجد) of Madīnah (مدينة) and a man walked in and they could see īmān (إيمان) in his face, Khushū’ (خشوع), So he with the gathering with these men that were sitting with him, in the masjid, when they saw this man coming in, they said this man is from Jannah (جنة), meaning this man belongs to Jannah, look at the īmān, look at the light in his face. This man prayed two Rakk’ah (ركعة) and they were too short rak’āt (ركعات). After he finished, Qais walked up to him and told him when you walked in, these men said this man belongs to Jannah. So, the man responded back by saying, we're talking here about ‘Abdullāh bin salām رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, the Jewish rabbi, who became Muslim. He said, No one ought to say what he doesn't know. What he means is how do they know that I'm from Jannah, why did they say that? But then, he gave Qais the explanation of why they said that? he said,

He said I saw a dream during the lifetime of Rasūlullāh ﷺ, I saw that I was in a garden and then he described the extension and the beauty of this garden. And in the centre of the garden, there was an iron pillar, The lower part of it was fixed in the earth and the upper end of it was in the sky. And at the top of this iron pillar, there was a ring-shaped handhold, So I heard the voice telling me to climb it, I said I can’t, then a man/servant came from behind me and lifted me up by my clothes until I climbed it and I was able to reach to the top of the pillar then I was told to grab on to that hand hold. So, I held it and I was told to hold it firmly. And I held it firmly and I woke up, holding it in my hand. So, I went to Rasūlullāh ﷺ and I narrated the dream to him. Rasūlullāh ﷺ told me that the garden is Islam and the handhold is the most trustworthy handle it is Islām (اسلام), it is the truth. And then Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, so you will remain as a Muslim till you die because he woke up holding on to it. So, the dream ended with him holding on firmly to that handhold. Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, you will die as a muslim, رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه.

There was another addition to his dream. In another Hadīth (حديث), he says, arabic He said, I came next to a mountain and I was told to climb that mountain. But whenever I tried to climb it, I would fall down. And I did that more than once and Rasūlullāh ﷺ interpreted this to mean that you will search for martyrdom, but you will not achieve it. And this is one of the miracles of Rasūlullāh ﷺ, it happened just as he told Abdullāh bin Salām, Abdullāh bin Salām died a natural death and not died as a Shahīd (شهيد).

Dream of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه for his Death: ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه saw a dream and this is in Musnad Imām Ahmad. He stood up on the mimbar (منبر) on Friday and After thanking Allāh ﷻ and making Salah (الصلاة) and Rasūlullāh ﷺ and mentioning the virtues of Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. he said, I saw a dream,

‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said, I saw a dream where a rooster would pick me twice. And the color of this rooster was red. The dream was narrated to Asmā bint ‘Umais رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها and she also used to interpret dreams. Asmā bint ‘Umais رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها was the wife of Ja’far Ibn abī Tālib رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, and then she married Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. So, she said ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه will be killed by a man who is non-Arab, and it occurred according to her interpretation, ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was killed by a Persian man named, Abu lu’lu’a al-Majūsī. So Asmā bint ‘Umais رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها also would interpret dreams, and ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه also knew that the meaning of this dream, it's a sign for his death.

Abū Mūsā al-asha’rī رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه also saw a dream about the death of ‘Umar bin al-Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه but he refused to tell him about it when they told him why? he said, I didn't want to give him the news of his death.

Dream Seen by Abū Sa’eed Al-Khudrī رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه for sajdah (سجدة) in Sūrah Sād (سورة صٓ): Abū Sa’eed Al-Khudrī رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه saw a dream that he was writing down the surah Sād (صٓ) and when he reached to the sajdah (سجدة) in Sūrah Sād (سورة صٓ), he said, he saw the pen and the ink and everything in this Presence making sujūd (سجود) and when he mentioned this dream to Rasūlullāh ﷺ, he said, Rasūlullāh ﷺ after that, would always make sujūd (سجود) at that āyah (آية).

Dream of ‘Uthmān bin ‘Affān رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه for his Martyrdom: ‘Uthmān bin ‘Affān رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه also saw a dream, the day in which he was killed. He saw a dream that Rasūlullāh ﷺ is telling him, you will have iftār with us you will break your Iftār with us. He was fasting that day, and he was killed that day, before he broke his fast, And subhān Allāh! The interpretation of his dream would be directly as he saw that he would have iftār that day with Rasūlullāh ﷺ.

Dream of At-Tufayl ibn Amr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه for himself and his Son: At-Tufayl ibn Amr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, another companion had a dream and this was before one of Al-Ghazwāt (الغزوات).

Arabic He said, I saw a dream. Tell me the interpretation. I saw that my hair was shaved, And I saw a bird come out from my mouth. And I saw that I was met by a woman and I entered into her womb. And I saw that my son was following me. But he was held back from me. They said this is a good dream In Shaa Allāh ان شآء الله)) he said, but I will tell you the interpretation. The shaving off my head means that my head would be cut and the bird that came out from my mouth means my soul will leave my body. And the woman that met me and I entered into her womb is the earth that I will be buried in and my son following me and trying to catch up with me but then he was held back means that he will try to die, A similar death to mine, meaning fī sabīlillāh (في سبيل الله) and immediately after that At-Tufayl رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was killed in Yammamah as a Shahīd (شهيد) and his son was injured a severe injury, but his injuries were healed. However, he was killed in the Battle of Al-Yarmūk (اليرموك), so the interpretation of the dream was exactly as At-Tufayl رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه mentioned.

Dream Seen for Al-Hussayn رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه Martyrdom: Al- ‘Abbās ibn Abdul-Muttalib رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه saw a dream, where Rasūlullāh ﷺ looked very exhausted and tired and his hair was ruffled and there was dust on Rasūlullāh ﷺ. Rasūlullāh ﷺ looked very tired in that dream. And he had the bottle in his hand and he was collecting blood from the ground and putting it in this bottle. So, I told Rasūlullāh ﷺ? What is this bottle? Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, this is the blood of Al-Hussayn and his companions. And I've been collecting it throughout this night. Ibn ‘Abbās رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was in Makah at the time and that Al-Hussayn رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was in ‘Irāq. So, it takes time for the news to arrive. When the news arrived, ibn ‘Abbās رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه asked about the particular day in which al Hussayn رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was killed and it turned out to be the same day when he saw that dream. And this is in Musnad Al-Imām Ahmad.

Dreams of As-Sālihīn (الصالحين): There are many dreams mentioned about As-Sālihīn (الصالحين) in the books of history. I'll mention just one dream because Alhamdulillāh it's sufficient to mention the dreams of Qur’ān (قرآن) and the dreams of Rasūlullāh ﷺ and the dreams of the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم. So, I'm not going to go deep in the issue of dreams of As-Sālihīn (الصالحين) because there's some exaggerations here and there and sometimes the narrations are not authentic. So, we'll leave that aside but I will mention one dream to you. And this dream relates to Al-Imām Muhammad bin Ismāīl al-Bukhārī رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه.

Al-Khatīb al-Baghdādī says in his book that one of the scholars, his name is Abdul Wāhid bin Ādam at-Tawawīsī رحمه الله. this scholar saw a dream at night he saw Rasūlullāh ﷺ with some of the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم and they were standing, waiting. So, I gave him salām (سلام), Rasūlullāh ﷺ responded back, I told him, Oh messenger of Allāh! Why are you standing there? Why are you waiting? Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, I am waiting for Muhammad bin Ismāīl al-Bukhārī. At-Tawawīsī رحمه الله said, the news reached to us of the death of Al-Imām Al-Bukhārī رحمه الله and it was the same day in which I saw that dream. so, these are examples of dreams seen by Rasūlullāh ﷺ and the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم and this dream seen by imām At-Tawawīsī رحمه الله.

How to Interpret Dreams: now next session In Shaa Allāh I'll go through examples of how to interpret dreams from the book of Ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله, will give examples of principles in dream interpretation. We'll go through the parts of the Book of Ibn Qutaybah al-Dīnawarī رحمه الله and probably I mentioned before, that Ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله is one of the earliest scholars of Islām (اسلام). He's a scholar of the third hijarī century and sometimes he was known as Hatīb Ahlus Sunnah wal Jammah, the orator of Ahlus Sunnah wal Jammah, he has a book on Dream Interpretation “Ta’bīr ar ru’yā” (تعبير الرؤيا)”. And probably it's one of the earlier books on the subject. It's a brief and concise book. And obviously if we want to study the whole book, it's gonna take time but I'm just gonna choose some bits and pieces from this book. And the objective is not to make the listener, a dream interpreter that would need much more study. But the objective is to give you a glimpse of the science of dream interpretation, and how it occurs.

Prerequisites for Dream Interpretation: In the beginning, he gives prerequisites for dream interpretation. What the dream interpreter needs to know. And he mentions that the person who will interpret dreams needs to have a good understanding of Qur’ān (قرآن) and he needs to also have a good understanding of Hadīth (حديث) and he needs to have a good understanding of language. And he needs to have a good understanding of famous parables and idioms and symbolic meanings that the word in a language carry. And then it gives some examples of direct dreams, dreams that do not need interpretation.

Dream Seen by ‘Āishah bin Talhahرضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها  to Change the Location of her Father’s Grave: For example, he mentions the dream that ‘Āishah bin Talhah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها had. ‘Āishah bin Talhahرضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنها  is the daughter of one of the ten who are given the glad tidings of Jannah (جنة), Talhah bin ‘Ubaydullillāh رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه. She saw a dream where her father was telling her change my place, and he already passed away. And he was telling his daughter in this dream, that he's asking them to change his location. So, when they dug up his grave, they found out that water started seeping into the grave. So, they change the location of his grave to a place that was dry. And by the way, they found out that his body did not change except some of his hair. But his body was protected Talhah bin ‘Ubaydillāh رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه died as a Shahīd (شهيد).

Another example is Abbā ibn Sa’d, one of the righteous men of this Ummah, he was riding in a boat, and he woke up and he said, I saw a dream that I was in Jannah and I was given milk and I drank from that milk. So, someone told him I asked you in the name of Allāh to vomit, and he did vomit and subhān Allāh milk did come out, even though there was no milk on this boat and there was no, there wasn't even any animal to provide milk, a goat or a cow or so. This is another example of a direct dream.

Interpreting Dreams from Qur’ānic Perspective: In the area of dream interpretation, the interpreter needs to have understanding of Qur’ān (قرآن) and then ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله gives examples of dream interpretation from Qur’ān (قرآن).

Allāh ﷻ says about Al-Munāfiqūn, Allāh ﷻ describes al-Munāfiqīn in sūrah Al-Munāfiqūn, Allāh ﷻ describes them as being like wood so he says that sometimes wood in a dream would mean nifāq (نفاق).

Rocks would Symbolise Harshness or Weak Religion in a Dream: And also, Allāh ﷻ says in Sūrah al-Baqarah.

And then your hearts were hardened after that, and they became like rocks, or even harder. So, rocks would symbolise harshness in a dream and they would symbolise weak religion.

A Ship Symbolises Safety: And then a ship which symbolises a safety because the people of Nūh عليه السلام were saved in a ship.

Water can Mean Fitnah: And water can mean fitnah because Allāh ﷻ says, Allāh ﷻ says we would have provided for them water as a fitnah for them.

Meat can represent Backbiting: Meat can represent backbiting, because Allāh ﷻ says in Sūrah Hujurāt, Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother's dead body? So, these are examples of how Qur’ān (قرآن) can help you in interpreting dreams.

A Key could mean Wealth: Also, a key could mean wealth, because Allāh ﷻ says about Qārūn, that the keys of Qārūn were heavy and it will need a group of men to carry, to carry just the keys, not the treasures, the keys of Qārūn.so these are examples of interpretation from Qur’ān (قرآن).

And then he talks about that that will be Hadīth (حديث), At’Ta’wīl bil hadīth (التأويل بالحديث) interpreting dreams from the Hadīth (حديث) of Rasūlullāh ﷺ.

A Crow or a Rat: So, Al-Ghurāb (الغراب) represents a corrupt evil person. Al-ghurāb is a Crow, and a rat would represent an evil or corrupt woman, because Rasūlullāh ﷺ called the ghurāb, fāsiq (فاسق), which means corrupt and he called the rat, fuwaysiqah (فويسقة) which is a feminine form of corrupt.

And qawarīr (قوارير), bottles of glass, they represent women because Rasūlullāh ﷺ said in a Hadīth (حديث), take it easy or be soft on the glass or the bottles and that were referring to women.

Interpreting Dreams according to Symbols: And the dream interpreter needs to also have an understanding of how certain words in the language have a symbolic meaning. For example, an eagle has a symbolic meaning of strength. That's why you would find that many nations, they use the eagle because the eagle is a symbol of strength. So, the interpretation of an eagle in a dream would mean a strong person.

Sometimes a certain thing Seen in a Dream could mean the Opposite: One of the amazing things in dreams is that some sometimes a certain thing that you see in a dream could mean the opposite.

Crying and Laughing: For example, if you see yourself crying, the interpretation of that is that you would be happy. If you see yourself laughing, then their interpretation of that would be that something would happen that would make you sad.

Fighting: If you see two people rustling or fighting, the winner loses and the loser wins, that's interpretation.

Grave and Prison: If you see someone in your dream entering into a grave, it means he will be in prison. If you see him entering a prison, it means that he would die. Obviously, most of the time, there’s no 100% rule, a rule that is applied all the time in dream interpretation and always the context needs to be looked at. We’ll go through some examples of what words symbolise.

Seeing Allāh ﷻ in Dream: What if you see Allāh ﷻ in your dream? He says, Arabic If you see Allāh ﷻ in your dream, then the place where you saw Allāh ﷻ, that place would be covered with justice, it will be a blessed place and provisions will be provided to the people of that place. This is if you see Allāh ﷻ. if you see the day of judgment that also means that justice will cover that place because the name of the Day of Judgment, judgment you derive from a justice, means that justice will cover that certain area.

Jannah and Hellfire: If a person sees that he is in Jannah, it could mean that a lot of rizq (رزق) will be provided to the people of that area or it could be a Glad tiding to that person that he would enter Jannah (جنة) And the opposite is true about hellfire.

Angels: Seeing angels in a dream, if you see angels in a particular area, it means that the people in that area will be victorious, or it means that they would be relieved from their pain, or it would mean that their problems would be solved. While if sometimes it could also mean especially if you see an angel carrying you, it would mean marginal.

The Sky: The sky the heavens, if you see that you climb into the sky and you disappeared. It could mean martyrdom, or it could mean that Allāh ﷻ would elevate your status.

Seeing Al-Ambiyā عليهم السلام: Seeing Al-Ambiyā عليهم السلام, there's a lot of details in this area. Every Nabī (نبي) if you see him, there's a different meaning. But in general, it is good. It is good to see any Nabī (نبي) in your dream. It is honour, it is a sign of good religion. Now if you see yourself turning into a Nabī (نبي), or you feel that you are a Nabi or you think that you're a Nabī (نبي) in your dream, it means that you will go through trials and tribulations just like the Ambiyā (أنبياء) did. And eventually you will prevail, eventually you will be rewarded. So, it's a good sign.

Seeing Oneself as a King: If a person sees himself turning into a king, or President in his dream, it means that he would succeed in duniyā (دنيا), but he would lose his religion.

Al-Ka’bah (الكعبة): What about seeing Al-Ka’bah (الكعبة) in a dream? If you are looking towards the Al-Ka’bah (الكعبة), you are looking at the leader of the Muslims because Al-Ka’bah (الكعبة) is the direction towards which Muslims face in their Salah. So, it symbolises leadership, it symbolises the focal point of the Muslims, so it stands for the Khalīfah (خليفة) or the leader of the ummah. If a person sees himself, praying towards Al-Ka’bah (الكعبة), it means that he is facing the right direction he's following the right path. If he also sees himself praying towards al qiblah (القبلة), it would mean the same thing. However, if a person sees himself, praying on top of Al-Ka’bah (الكعبة), that means he has lost his religion. And if a person sees himself praying but he is deviating from the direction of qiblah (قبلة), then he has deviated from the religion and according to how much his deviation is from Qiblah (قبلة), that’s how much he has deviated from Islam. And if a person sees himself praying opposite the direction of Qiblah (قبلة), this is a sign that the person is completely on the wrong track.

Reading Qur’ān (قرآن): If the person sees himself reading Qur’ān (قرآن) in dream that's a good sign. It is Hikmah (حكمة) and then it depends on the particular Surah or ayah which the person reads, recites, it could have a special meaning. This is about Qur’ān (قرآن). If a person sees himself as an Imam, he's leading others in prayer. This means he will assume a position of responsibility in duniyā (دنيا) because the Imam leaves the people in Salah. So, it symbolises leadership.

The Sun, the Moon and Stars: Seeing the sun, the moon and stars, the sun stands for the king or the leader of that particular area. And the moon represents the second in leadership, like the vice president or the Wazīr (وزير) of the king. Now, you can see here that the sun and the moon carry a different meaning than the meaning we saw in the Sūrah (سورة) of Yusuf because in Sūrah Yūsuf, the interpretation of the dream that Yūsuf عليه السلام had, when he saw the sun, the moon and eleven stars making sujūd (سجود) to him that represented his father, mother and brothers pledging their respect to him. And that actually occurred when they entered into Egypt. And they actually did make sujūd (سجود) to him, Physically, they did make sujūd (سجود) to him, and making sujūd (سجود) in those days was allowed to something that was made harām (حرام) by Muhammad ﷺ. Rasūlullāh ﷺ said that it's only appropriate for a Muslim to make sujūd (سجود) to Allāh ﷻ but before Muhammad ﷺ in the Sharī’ah (شريعة) of Yūsuf عليه السلام, it was allowed for people to make sujūd (سجود), out of respect, for as we see, they did sujūd (سجود) of respect, this is not sujūd (سجود) of ‘ibadah this is sujūd (سجود) of respect to Yūsuf عليه السلام, but the sun and the moon over there represented his father and mother.

Yes, in a dream the sun and the moon can also represent the father or mother but they could also represent the leaders in that particular area. If you see the sun setting and disappearing, it could mean the death of the leader in that area. If you see weakness in the light of the sun, or the colour is reddish or it is being covered by a cloud, that would also mean a calamity or difficulty that would befall the leader in that area. And then it talks about seeing the different parts of the body. What does the head mean? What does the hand mean? What does the foot mean? And we will skip that section.

Marriage: The next section he talks about marriage. He says if you see yourself marrying a woman, then according to her beauty, that is how much wealth you would receive in this duniyā (دنيا). So usually seeing a beautiful woman is a good sign in a dream. Obviously, this is talking about when you see a woman but there's no wet dream involved. Any wet dream has no interpretation whatsoever. There is no meaning in those dreams at all. they're meaningless.

Dead Person: Seeing dead person. If that person speaks to you, then usually his words don't need any interpretation. They carry the direct meaning of those words. They don't need to be interpreted.

The scholars of interpretation say that the speech of children, animals and the dead are true, and don't need any interpretation. The meaning is direct, because they don't lie. The dead person is in Ākhirah (اٰخرة), so he won't lie and animals, when they speak, they will speak the truth. And they say the same thing with children. If you see a child speaking to you in your dream, then the words are true and direct.

If a dead person takes away something from you in your dream that means you would lose that thing. If you see yourself embracing a dead person, it means that you would have a long life.

If you see yourself entering into a grave and you are alive, it means imprisonment. But if a person sees himself being imprisoned in an unknown place, then it could mean death.

If a person sees himself with dead people, it means that he is accompanying Munāfiqīn (منافقين), because the munāfiq (منافق) has a dead heart. If you see a dead person that you know and he is happy, it could represent his situation in Ākhirah (اٰخرة). If you see dead person tired, exhausted, afraid it could stand for his position in Al-ākhirah (الآخرة). if you see yourself walking behind that dead person, following him, wherever he goes, it would mean that you would follow the way of that particular person.

Next, he talks about “bāb ta’wīl Ru’yāt al Amtār "(باب تأويل رؤية الامطار), rain. if you see rain, and it's localised. So, you see the rain falling on a particular area, but surrounding that area, there's no rain. This rain could be a rain of punishment that would befall the people of that area. But you we see a general rain. So, wherever you look, you can see rain, that rain is mercy. It is blessing from Allāh ﷻ and it is assistance from Allāh.

So, for example, if a prisoner sees such rain, it would mean that he would be freed from his prison. If an ill person sees such rain, it could mean that he would be healed from his illness. So, it is mercy from Allāh ﷻ. Also, you might remember we talked about the dream that was interpreted by Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه here he saw the sky raining honey, and butter and he interpreted it to mean Islām (اسلام) and the benefit that people are getting from Qur’ān (قرآن).

I might have also mentioned that the sea represents the sovereignty of the state, a lake or sea. So, if a person sees himself swimming in the sea and he's a prisoner and he reaches to the shore and he walks out of the sea, it means that he would be freed from jail.

Interpretation of Trees and Animals: Then he talks about the interpretation of trees, animals, trees, animals, represent people and they all represent people, according to the nature of the particular tree and the nature of that animal.

Harmful Animals: So, for example, if you see a harmful animal, an animal that we as human beings, perceive as being harmful, such as a snake, this would represent an enemy, human being. If you see a scorpion, it's an enemy.

A Cow or a Goat: But if you see, let's say a goat, or you see a cow, it could represent a good person because Rasūlullāh ﷺ saw in his dream, cows that are being slaughtered. He said, these are my companions, that would be killed in the Battle of Uhud (احد), because we as human beings perceive cattle as being beneficial to us. So, a cow would represent a good person in a dream.

Weapons: Weapons represent protection.

Fire: Fire could stand for war.

Clouds: Clouds represent wisdom.

A Horse: A horse, if you see yourself riding a horse, it would mean honour and position in this duniyā (دنيا) that is, if the horse is controllable, so you can control it. But if the horse is running wildly with you on its back, and you cannot control it, this could mean that the person is following their hawā (هوآء), They're following their whims and desires and is taking them in all different directions and it is an uncontrollable situation, So it's a bad sign. But if the horse is under control, then it means you will receive a position in this duniyā (دنيا) according to how nice and strong, that horse is.

Flying: If you see yourself flying or you're holding on to a bird and it's carrying you somewhere, it would mean travel.

A Camel: Then he talks about a camel, he also says it represents a man. If you see yourself fighting camel, then you might be fighting with an enemy. He talks then about goats and sheep, Same thing. He gives a lot of details; I will not mention all of them and it could get a bit confusing.

A Snake: But he talks about the snake and he says that it represents an enemy that is hiding, its animosity towards you and then he says that the white snake is weaker than the dark snake. And if you see yourself killing that snake, then you will win. But if the snake bites you, then that enemy will harm you according to how bad the bite was. And the scorpion is an enemy that usually harms with its tongue. So, it's an enemy that will harm you with its words.

Lion, Tiger or Wolf: Lion is an enemy that's very strong, tiger, same thing. Wolf, these are all enemies, but he says that the fox has many meanings in a dream.

A Bee and a Fly: A Bee is good, it symbolises rizq (رزق), but flies are weak enemies. Same thing with mosquitoes.

A Frog and a Turtle: Frog is a worshiper, ‘ābid (عابد), so frog is a good sign. Same thing with a turtle, they carry good meaning.

Miscellaneous Issues: Then he moves on to other miscellaneous issues, he talks about light means guidance. Darkness means misguidance, if you see an area and it looks like the area's haunted and it's destroyed, it means that there's misguidance in that particular area.

If you see a place that is very well built, but then it falls down in your dream, it means that calamities would be fallen that particular area.

Says, if a person sees that he is deaf or dumb, that would mean a weakness in religion.

If a person sees himself old in age while he is young, that is wisdom. And if you see that, you will miss the Salah and you're not able to find the place to pray, that means that you will go through some difficulties.

If you see yourself making wudhū (وضو), that means that whatever problem you are going through, when you saw the dream, that problem will be solved. If you see yourself making wudhu (وضو) but you didn't finish the wudū (وضو), It means that that problem will be solved according to how much wudū (وضو) you finished.

If a dā’ī (داعي), a person who's calling to Islām (اسلام), sees himself singing, or he's using musical instruments such as a guitar, or a flute, or any other instrument, even though what appears to have a bad meaning but the meaning is good, It means that his words would have an effect on the people because Hassan al Basrī رحمه الله dream was seen for him that he was standing naked on a dumpster, and he was singing on a barbat (بربت), it is something similar to a guitar, but some old fashioned instrument, all of the signs in this dream do not appear to be good, naked and standing on a dumpster and singing but Ibn Sirīn رحمه الله interpreted the dream to have very good meaning. He said naked, Al Hassan al-Basrī رحمه الله standing naked means, he is free of sins and standing on a dumpster means duniyā (دنيا) is under his feet, and he's standing on top of it, meaning duniyā (دنيا) does not control him. And using this musical instrument, which is similar to a guitar means his words have an effect on the ears of the listeners just like music does.

But Ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله says that also these musical instruments could have another meaning and that is a calamity, that would befall that area.

If you see yourself in a green garden and then all of that greenery disappeared, it means that some evil befalls on a person who saw such a dream.

If a person sees himself on a swing means that he's playing with his religion, means going back and forth.

If a person sees that he is sweeping his house, it could mean that he would lose his money.

If a person sees that he was being called from an unknown location, and responded to the call, it could mean that he would die.

If a person sees that he is sleeping under a tree, it could mean that he would have a lot of children.

If you see a minaret falling down, it means that the people of that Masjid will dispute among themselves and disunite.

If you see yourself holding a pen, or writing with a pen, it could mean knowledge.

If you see yourself gathering pearls, it could mean that you are also seeking knowledge and you are learning this knowledge.

If you see doors opening up in the heavens, it could mean rain falling down from the sky.

If you see yourself knocking on a door, it could mean that your du’ā (دعا) will be accepted.

These are examples from the book of dream interpretation by Ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله. I hope that you found some benefit in it. Again, I said obviously just reading a book does not make a person, a dream interpreter but it gives you a flavour of this interesting world of al-ghayb (الغيب) of the unseen, which Rasūlullāh ﷺ said, it is the glad tiding that a Muslim received in this duniyā (دنيا). by this we end this series of lectures. we ask Allāh ﷻ to benefit us all.
